versions.stem: Most experiments involving electrolysis use inert electrodes, which do not take part in the reactions. However, in some experiments the electrodes do take part in the reactions. She uses this method. weigh two clean strips of copper use one strip as the positive electrode and the other as the negative electrode after electrolysis wash the strips of copper with ethanol (a liquid that boils at $ 7 8^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $) dry the strips of copper and reweigh them The ionic half-equations for the reactions at the electrodes are Positive electrode $\mathrm {C u} (\mathrm {s}) - 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {C u} ^ {2 +} (\mathrm {a q})$ Negative electrode $\mathrm {C u} ^ {2 +} (\mathrm {a q}) + 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {C u} (\mathrm {s})$ A student investigates the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution using copper electrodes which do take part in the reaction. She uses this apparatus.
